key_insight: A shallow variational quantum circuit can learn the quantum phase estimation measurement distribution analytically from the Dirichlet kernel, avoiding expensive quantum circuit simulation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a hardware-efficient route to molecular energy estimation on NISQ devices by replacing deep QPE circuits with a linearly scalable surrogate that still reaches chemical accuracy.
method: Compute the QPE target distribution classically from the FCI ground-state energy, ancilla count, and evolution time using the Dirichlet kernel.
Train a shallow VQC to match that distribution on IBM Quantum hardware, testing entangler layouts, depths, and dynamical decoupling.
Evaluate performance with Hellinger distance, fidelity error, total variation distance, and Jensen-Shannon divergence across staged experiments.
evidence_signal: Across staged IBM Quantum experiments on H2, the linear-entangler ansatz with one VQC layer performed best under noise and recovered the ground-state energy within chemical accuracy.
watch_item: The approach is validated on a small molecular benchmark, so scaling to larger systems and more complex Hamiltonians may require new tuning and robustness checks.
paper_title: An Analytically Trained Variational Surrogate for Quantum Phase Estimation on NISQ Hardware
